title: Psalm 51: Create in Me a Clean Heart
summary: David pleads for mercy after his sin with Bathsheba, appealing to God's loving devotion and great compassion. He confesses his guilt without excuse, asks to be washed, purified, and made new, and prays not to lose God's presence or Holy Spirit. He promises to teach sinners God's ways and offers God what he truly desires, a broken and contrite heart, before closing with a prayer for Jerusalem.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 6
from.text: From early in Christian history the church grouped Psalm 6 with Psalms 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, and 143 as the seven Penitential Psalms, prayed especially in times of repentance and during Lent.

line: David's plea for mercy after his sin with Bathsheba: confession without excuse, a prayer to be washed and made new, and the broken and contrite heart God will not despise.
guide: Pray it with no excuse in it, naming the wrong and leaning your whole weight on God's mercy. Ask, as verse 10 does, to be changed as well as forgiven. If you fear you have gone too far, remember who first prayed it.

care.text: If you have been harmed by someone with power over you, hear this too. What was done to you was wrong, and it was not your fault. The Bible did not blame Bathsheba, and it does not blame you. Please tell someone you trust. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: A plea for mercy and cleansing
Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow
A clean heart and a right spirit
Praise and the sacrifice of a broken heart

verses.t: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
In Your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar.
